FMPSI26 is approaching, and I need to think about what I want to work on. I would like to implement some basic ergodic optimisation.

In this context, I consider functions which may take (positive or negative) infinite values, and integrate them against (nonnegative) measures. In other words, integrating EReal-valued functions.

It seems there is a relatively straightforward way to do this (take the positive/negative part, cast as ENNReal, lintegrate, cast as EReal, subtract). However, I am not well-versed on this part of Mathlib, and I couldn't find anything. Is it something which already exists or not? Is it desirable or to be avoided?

Paging @Sébastien Gouëzel and @Floris van Doorn.

I don't think we have anything on this. The reason is that the theory is not well behaved: a function has a meaningful integral when either its positive part or its negative part is integrable, but this means that the sum of two functions with meaningful integral might not have a meaningful integral itself.

So I think your approach separating the positive and negative parts is the right one, and I'm afraid the theorem will be a little bit messy to state properly. But that's just a fact of life, and EReal-valued integrals are definitely useful, so it's not a reason not to do it.
We have an implementation of that (messy) integral with @Gaëtan Serré. I'll link to it in a few hours.
I think messy is a understatement in this case :sweat_smile:

I've also wanted this integral for a student project related to subharmonic functions. We don't have anything like this in Mathlib, and we're working around not having this.
I'm a bit worried about the amount of code duplication this would entail if we (properly) want to incorporate this into Mathlib... But that is no reason to have this.

One related thing I've been thinking about: it should be possible to define the Bochner integral for an ENormedSpace, i.e. a docs#ENormedAddCommMonoid that is a module over docs#NNReal.

class ENormedSpace (E : Type*) [TopologicalSpace E] extends ENormedAddCommMonoid E, Module ℝ≥0 E where
  enorm_smul_eq_smul : ∀ (c : ℝ≥0) (x : E), ‖c • x‖ₑ = c • ‖x‖ₑ

(perhaps with more axioms)
It will be a lot of work to do this, since the Bochner integral depends on quite some functional analysis, which would then also have to be generalized to ENormedSpace, but I don't expect mathematical obstructions.

Doing this would have multiple advantages:

  • Bochner integral for EReal-valued functions
  • nicer transition theorems between Bochner and Lebesgue integration (they match if the function is integrable)
  • The ability to stop using the Lebesgue integral altogether, if you don't mind proving a few extra integrability conditions.

I'm not convinced that the generalization you're pointing to would help with EReal-valued integrals: the generalization of the Bochner integral would only make sense for integrable functions, i.e., the integral would have to be finite, while to me the main interest of the EReal-valued integral is that it can take the value +\infty (for a function whose negative part is integrable and whose positive part is not integrable) or -\infty.

And I don't think we will ever stop using the Lebesgue integral: one of its main points is that it does take the value +\infty, and so it applies to functions which are not integrable. Just in the same way that series in ENNReal are always summable, this is extremely helpful (for instance in Carleson).

Lebesgue integral also gives sensible values to non measurable functions which does have applications.

But I imagine that Damien's case might be similar to a thread we had asking about this a while back asking about an EReal integral where you want to take a supremum over the integrals of a set of functions f. And you except many of them to have negative infinity integral (and you couldn't use the junk value 0 since this may mess up the sup). I am sure there are hacky ways to get around this but in the long run it seems like its worth having this kind of integral.

found the thread: #mathlib4 > On Potentially Formalizing Donsker Varadhan

I imagine this is related to why @Rémy Degenne and @Gaëtan Serré worked on it?

I'm finally at a computer and made the repository public: https://github.com/RemyDegenne/e-values . The integral is in the file https://github.com/RemyDegenne/e-values/blob/main/EValues/EIntegral.lean .

The repository contains a formalization of theory related to e-variables, a relatively new statistical object.
We're planning to move it to the new Statlib, but we'd like to finish the proof of existence of the numeraire first (an e-variable with maximal log utility).

We could PR the integral for EReal to Mathlib (but it needs some cleaning first).

David Ledvinka said:

found the thread: #mathlib4 > On Potentially Formalizing Donsker Varadhan

I imagine this is related to why Rémy Degenne and Gaëtan Serré worked on it?

It's not exactly this, but it's not completely unrelated either: there is a form of duality between e-variables and Kullback-Leibler divergences.

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

I'm not convinced that the generalization you're pointing to would help with EReal-valued integrals: the generalization of the Bochner integral would only make sense for integrable functions, i.e., the integral would have to be finite, while to me the main interest of the EReal-valued integral is that it can take the value +\infty (for a function whose negative part is integrable and whose positive part is not integrable) or -\infty.

Oh, that is a good point. That seems tricky/impossible to achieve with just the data of a ENormedSpace.

And I don't think we will ever stop using the Lebesgue integral: one of its main points is that it does take the value +\infty, and so it applies to functions which are not integrable. Just in the same way that series in ENNReal are always summable, this is extremely helpful (for instance in Carleson).

I should have clarified: I think it would be possible in a particular project. I (of course) don't want to get rid of it in Mathlib. And as you rightfully point out, it might be easier to work with the Lebesgue integral even if you're guaranteed to only work with integrable functions.

@David Ledvinka : Yes, I am dealing with a similar issue. Thank you for the link to the older discussion, and thanks to everybody for this input.

At the moment, it seems the best is to wait for some implementation of what @Rémy Degenne wrote. It would be useless for me to try to re-write the same thing in a worse way.
